gate: Most people mistake this code for a problem in the room. Two people warm to each other, then something rubs, and the conclusion comes quickly: we are not a fit. The code is friction, and friction is what it does. The rub is not a sign that intimacy has gone wrong. It is the gate doing its work, surfacing the edges where two emotional fields actually meet. A person carrying this code feels it as a heat that rises near closeness, sometimes a flare, sometimes a slow simmer that takes hours to read. The pull toward another and the snag against another come from the same place. To soften the friction away is to soften the gate away, and what is left is politeness with no real contact. The gate is built rough on purpose, because real intimacy needs an edge to form against.
centre_field: Sit with where this code lives in the body-map. It sits in the emotional centre, the seat of feeling, the only place on the chart that is both a motor and an awareness. That double nature is the teaching. Feeling here is not a passing weather event. It is fuel, and it carries information at the same time. Friction inside that centre is not noise to clear. It is the wave doing what a wave does, lifting and dropping, and the clarity is on the other side of waiting it out. The centre runs on time. The gate inside it cannot be read in the moment of heat. Decisions made at the crest are almost always the wrong shape. Read in the trough, they come out true. The centre is asking for patience the moment friction shows up, not a verdict.
channel: Friction by itself has no destination. It reaches across to the gate of sexuality, and the two together form the channel of mating. The reach is the whole point. Friction without the other side is just heat, an emotional charge that loops back on itself and turns to argument or withdrawal. The sexuality gate is what gives the friction a body to meet, a barrier to cross, a closeness to actually arrive at. Joined, the code becomes the work of bonding, the slow breaking down of the wall that keeps two people separate. Alone, this gate scratches at intimacy without finding it. With its partner, the friction has somewhere to go. The code wants the other side. It is built to need a barrier to dissolve, and a person to dissolve it with.
